diagnosis: Loss of pod policy-routing rules after a systemd-networkd restart explains cross-node connectivity loss. The restart is the likely trigger; the precise rule-removal behavior is not demonstrated.
missing_checks: Identify the CNI and networkd version/configuration, affected policy-routing tables, and whether restoring the missing rules restores cross-node traffic.

diagnosis: Removal of the inter-worker firewall allow rule blocks cross-node pod traffic.
missing_checks: Confirm rejected flow tuples match the affected pod path and that restoring the intended rule restores connectivity.

diagnosis: Cross-node dataplane failure is localized, but its cause cannot be determined from pod readiness and same-node success alone.
missing_checks: Compare routes and policy rules before/after maintenance.
Inspect inter-worker firewall, NetworkPolicy, CNI/tunnel state and packet captures.

diagnosis: Synchronized node-agent startup produced a burst of large unpaginated pod LIST requests and API-server memory pressure, explaining the API degradation.
missing_checks: Measure response sizes, API-server memory/GC and termination events to distinguish pressure from confirmed OOM termination.
Verify rollout concurrency and actual LIST request scope.

diagnosis: Severe etcd storage fsync latency during a storage snapshot is the supported control-plane bottleneck; the node-agent rollout is coincidental.
missing_checks: Correlate etcd commit/request latency and disk utilization with the snapshot and recovery.

diagnosis: Temporal overlap between a rollout and API latency does not identify the bottleneck.
missing_checks: Inspect API request volume/size, server resource use and errors.
Inspect etcd latency, storage metrics and rollout start concurrency.

diagnosis: A template condition rendered the desired resource set empty, and automated GitOps pruning deleted the previously managed resources.
missing_checks: Confirm the deleted resource identities match the missing Services and determine which template input changed.

diagnosis: A cleanup service account deleted the affected namespaces, causing deletion of their Services.
missing_checks: Inspect namespace deletion lifecycle and cleanup job/audit attribution to determine why the delete was issued.

diagnosis: Services are absent, but the deleting actor and initiating configuration change are unknown.
missing_checks: Inspect Service and namespace DELETE audit events.
Compare GitOps desired manifests, prune history and infrastructure/cleanup change history.

diagnosis: The Service selector excludes healthy old pods, concentrating traffic on two new pods; this overload is the supported explanation for their OOM/restart loop and rollout disruption.
missing_checks: Correlate new-pod memory with request rate and compare resource limits.
Inspect EndpointSlice readiness conditions and request distribution during restarts.

diagnosis: The new image has workload-dependent memory growth absent in the previous image under equal load; an image-level memory regression explains the OOM failures.
missing_checks: Compare limits, runtime settings and heap/RSS profiles to identify the regression; continuous RSS growth alone does not establish a specific leak.

diagnosis: New pods are OOMKilled, but uneven traffic, changed limits and a memory regression remain unresolved alternatives.
missing_checks: Inspect Service selectors, EndpointSlice readiness and per-pod load.
Compare image/configuration/limits and run controlled equal-load memory comparisons.

diagnosis: Deletion of the shared instance profile prevents replacement provisioning and is consistent with existing workers losing renewable credentials after cached credentials expire.
missing_checks: Inspect preceding RemoveRoleFromInstanceProfile events and instance associations; successful profile deletion requires removal of its role.
Check metadata credential refresh failures and actual credential expiry times on affected workers.
technical_inconsistencies: The normalized deletion event omits required role-removal prerequisites. This is incomplete lifecycle evidence, not a contradiction if those actions occurred.

diagnosis: A 19-minute node clock skew causes signed cloud API requests to expire, explaining cloud credential/signature errors and plausibly bootstrap failure.
missing_checks: Verify the same skew and RequestExpired failure on replacement nodes, and confirm time correction restores bootstrap.

diagnosis: Credential errors and failed node initialization do not distinguish deleted IAM resources, denied permissions, expired credentials, clock skew or metadata/network failure.
missing_checks: Inspect exact cloud errors, IAM audit/profile state, credential expiry/refresh, node time and bootstrap logs.

diagnosis: The load balancer lost its Redis backend endpoint during scaling despite the pod remaining available; the blocked eviction and endpoint removal expose inconsistent lifecycle handling.
missing_checks: Inspect controller/version and scaling sequence to establish why endpoint removal preceded or outlived the blocked eviction.
Verify backend reattachment restores load-balancer reachability.

diagnosis: A newly selecting ingress NetworkPolicy denies the client namespace access to Redis; policy drops and direct-IP failure support this mechanism.
missing_checks: Confirm load-balancer forwarding preserves or translates client identity in a way covered by the observed policy drops.

diagnosis: The fault is somewhere on the client-to-load-balancer-to-pod path; Running/Ready status does not identify it.
missing_checks: Test direct pod connectivity from affected clients and inspect LB target membership/health.
Inspect policies, firewall paths and packet captures.

diagnosis: An obsolete bundled CA store cannot validate new TLS connections after its trusted root expires; established old connections conceal the problem until reconnection.
missing_checks: Inspect the actual chain, client verification implementation and alternate chain/root supplied by the current CA store.

diagnosis: The new deployment uses login.internal while the presented certificate covers auth.internal, producing hostname validation failure.
missing_checks: Inspect the configured endpoint/SNI and full SAN list, then verify correction of endpoint or certificate restores connections.

diagnosis: Success on established connections does not distinguish a trust-chain failure from hostname, certificate, DNS or new-connection configuration problems.
missing_checks: Capture the exact handshake error and chain/SANs.
Compare endpoint/SNI, CA bundles and fresh connections from both deployments.

diagnosis: Recursive fsGroup ownership changes over millions of files delay volume preparation and application startup.
missing_checks: Inspect effective fsGroupChangePolicy and CSI ownership behavior to select an applicable mitigation.

diagnosis: A stale attachment to the previous NotReady node blocks attachment of the volume to the replacement, preventing startup.
missing_checks: Inspect access mode, VolumeAttachment/controller state and safe fencing/detachment conditions on the old node.

diagnosis: File count is a potential clue but does not prove filesystem ownership traversal or any other startup blocker.
missing_checks: Inspect pod events and kubelet/CSI attach/mount logs.
Check init containers, image pulls, volume attachment state and ownership traversal progress.

diagnosis: The metrics collector inspection causes memory-map lock contention and request stalls; the isolated disable/re-enable experiment supplies causal support.
missing_checks: Identify the inspected proc interface, kernel/runtime version and lock stacks to select a targeted fix.

diagnosis: Stop-the-world garbage collection causes the tail-latency spikes; allocation reduction removes them with collector settings unchanged.
missing_checks: Inspect GC pause traces, allocation profiles and runtime settings to identify the triggering allocation behavior.

diagnosis: Rare latency spikes with moderate average CPU do not identify their cause.
missing_checks: Capture slow-request traces and profiles, GC pauses, CPU throttling/scheduling latency, I/O and collector timing.

diagnosis: Stale UDP conntrack translations retain a removed CoreDNS endpoint for affected flows, blackholing their DNS requests.
missing_checks: Identify dataplane/kube-proxy behavior and conntrack cleanup timing; validate recovery of the affected flow after its stale mapping is removed.

diagnosis: A new egress NetworkPolicy blocks affected clients’ UDP DNS traffic to live CoreDNS endpoints.
missing_checks: Check whether apparent intermittency is across clients, policy timing or cached/TCP-fallback queries; a fixed deny generally consistently blocks matching UDP flows.

diagnosis: Healthy CoreDNS replicas and a subset of failing clients do not distinguish stale conntrack, policy, client resolver issues or local dataplane problems.
missing_checks: Compare DNS EndpointSlices and failing-flow conntrack destinations.
Capture packets and inspect policy drops, CoreDNS load and client resolver behavior.

diagnosis: Fail-open admission before CA injection plausibly placed the simulation on a real node. The alleged later rejection of pod/status updates due to injected nodeSelector/labels is not sufficiently coherent to establish the cleanup failure mechanism.
missing_checks: Obtain the exact admission response, JSONPatch, API rejection message and HTTP status.
Confirm the webhook matches pods/status and inspect the Kubernetes version/status update strategy.
Determine whether the patch is malformed, denied by admission, or changes some independently invalid status/metadata field; inspect whether completion status actually persisted.
technical_inconsistencies: Ordinary pod/status update processing restores the existing Pod spec before status validation, so a nodeSelector spec mutation alone does not establish the claimed immutable-spec rejection.
Labels are not intrinsically an invalid Pod metadata change. A concrete rejection reason is needed; the stated fields do not by themselves explain rejected completion updates.

diagnosis: An orphaned cleanup finalizer blocks deletion of an already Succeeded pod because the responsible cleanup controller is absent.
missing_checks: Confirm deletionTimestamp and finalizer ownership, and determine whether required external cleanup has completed before finalizer removal.

diagnosis: Process exit alone does not establish persisted Pod completion or successful cleanup; remaining Pods can also be normal without a deletion policy.
missing_checks: Inspect Pod phase/container statuses, deletionTimestamp, finalizers and controller events/logs.
Inspect admission errors and the expected simulation cleanup lifecycle.

diagnosis: A stale fixed package repository URL returns 404 and aborts bootstrap on the four instances, preventing their registration and leaving insufficient cluster capacity.
missing_checks: Test bootstrap using the current package path and verify nodes register and become Ready.

diagnosis: The new instance role is absent from the cluster authentication mapping, so kubelet registration is rejected despite successful network/bootstrap prerequisites.
missing_checks: Verify the exact identity presented by kubelet and the cluster authentication mechanism, then validate registration after the intended mapping is restored.

diagnosis: The cloud instances have not joined Kubernetes; the evidence does not distinguish incomplete bootstrap, network reachability, authentication or kubelet failure.
missing_checks: Inspect bootstrap and kubelet registration logs on missing instances.
Check package installation, API endpoint connectivity, identity mapping and node startup progress.
